To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a neurite-promoting substance from rat RN22 Schwannoma cells is immunologically and biochemically related to laminin and that the neurite-promotion activity of the substance is blocked by antibodies raised against laminin but not against the neurite-promoter itself.
a neurite-promoting macromolecular factor isolated from the growth medium of rat RN22 schwannomas has immunoreactivity and molecular weight characteristics similar to those of laminin.
rat schwannoma cells release a neurite-promoting protein into their growth medium and that this protein is a form of laminin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the isolation and partial characterization of a neurite-promoting protein from the rat schwann cell line RN22.
a neurite-promoting substance released by RN22 rat schwannoma cells.
the identification of the schwann cell-derived neurite-promoting substance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the schwannoma cell factor has the properties of laminin, but that it is not identical to laminin and probably represents a modified or processed form of laminin.
the schwannoma neuritic-promoting factor is a mixture of rat laminin and proteoglycan.
the purified rat RN22 schwann cell factor contains a major component with the same immunoreactivity, electrophoretic mobility, and morphology as rat laminin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rat schwannomma factor is a macromolecular mixture containing laminin and proteoglycains.
the neurite- stimulating factor isolated from the conditioned medium of rat RN22 schwannomas contains a major laminin component and a minor proteoglycan component.
a macromolecular schwannoma factor has been purified from RN22 schwannomas and that this factor contains laminin and proteoglycana.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neurite-promotion activity released by rat RN22 schwannomas into their growth medium is due to laminin.
the neurite- stimulating factor from RN22 rat schwannoma cells appears to contain laminin as well as other molecules that may be important for neurite regeneration.
the neurite- stimulating activity released by rat RN22 schwannomas into their growth medium is associated with the laminin immunoreactive protein.
